facts.text: A heavy off-road machine is a very large, very heavy vehicle built to move earth, rock or materials on a job site rather than travel on public roads.
facts.quote: A heavy off-road machine is a very large, very heavy vehicle built to move earth, rock or materials on a job site rather than to travel on public roads.

facts.text: Heavy off-road machines are called earth-moving machinery in international standards, mobile plant in Britain and Australia, and heavy mobile equipment in the United States.
facts.quote: Engineers group them under names such as earth-moving machinery (the term in the international standards), mobile plant (Britain and Australia) or heavy mobile equipment (United States).

facts.text: Manufacturer figures put the Volvo A60 articulated hauler at about 44 t empty and 99 t loaded.
facts.quote: manufacturer figures for a Volvo A60 articulated hauler at about 44 t empty and 99 t loaded

facts.text: Manufacturer figures put the Caterpillar D11 dozer at about 107 t.
facts.quote: a Caterpillar D11 dozer at about 107 t

facts.text: Manufacturer figures put the Caterpillar 797F mining truck at about 624 t fully loaded.
facts.quote: a Caterpillar 797F mining truck at about 624 t fully loaded

facts.text: Heavy off-road machines work on gravel, mud, snow, loose rock and steep slopes, where stopping depends on the ground as much as on the brakes.
facts.quote: These machines work on gravel, mud, snow, loose rock and steep slopes, where stopping depends on the ground as much as on the brakes.

facts.text: Close-contact work is part of heavy off-road machine operation: loaders drive right up to piles, and trucks back up to the edge of dumps.
facts.quote: a loader is supposed to drive right up to a pile, and a truck is supposed to back up to the edge of a dump. Closeness is part of the job.

facts.text: One manufacturer's heavy off-road machines may work across 100 or more job sites and applications.
facts.quote: One manufacturer's machines may work across 100 or more job sites and applications

facts.text: Most heavy off-road machine platforms have 10 or more critical operating scenarios.
facts.quote: most platforms have 10 or more critical operating scenarios

facts.text: Sensor types, numbers and mounting positions differ by heavy off-road machine platform.
facts.quote: sensor types, numbers and mounting positions differ by platform [Introduction].

facts.text: Wheeled, tracked and articulated heavy off-road machines stop differently.
facts.quote: Wheeled, tracked and articulated machines stop differently

facts.text: Brake standards treat wheeled, tracked and articulated heavy off-road machines in separate documents.
facts.quote: Wheeled, tracked and articulated machines stop differently, and the brake standards treat them in separate documents [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Long stopping distances are a validation concern for automatic braking on heavy off-road machines because of their mass, ground conditions and close-contact work.
facts.quote: Everything about validating an automatic brake on these machines follows from their mass, their ground and their close-contact work: stopping distances are long

facts.text: Heavy off-road machine brakes are limited by heat and torque, which matters for automatic-brake validation.
facts.quote: brakes are limited by heat and torque

facts.text: Load shifting matters for validating automatic braking on heavy off-road machines.
Many real heavy off-road machine tasks look like a collision to a sensor, which matters for automatic-brake validation.
facts.quote: many real tasks look like a collision to a sensor.

facts.text: Transferring evidence proven only for road vehicles to quarry operation is a central uncertainty of the heavy off-road automatic-braking validation program; the booklet labels such evidence "on-road evidence".
facts.quote: The booklet marks evidence proven only for road vehicles as "on-road evidence" because the step from a highway to a quarry is one of the central uncertainties of the program [Introduction].
